lesson_title: Finance and Data Essentials: The Final Exam Revision Run
hook_text: One blackout-week mark dragged his average down 9,5 points. The median never flinched.
clip_script: Five marks in the homework book: 68, 64, 75, 71 — and one disaster, 22, from the week the power was out every evening. His aunt adds them up: 300 divided by 5 — he's a 60 learner, she says. But arrange the marks first: 22, 64, 68, 71, 75. The middle one — the median — is 68. So who's telling the truth? Take the blackout mark away and the mean of the rest jumps to 69,5. ONE bad mark dragged the mean down nine and a half points, while the median never moved — because the median only cares about position, not how bad the bad mark was. That's a full exam answer: name the outlier, say which way it pulls. Now the till: a slip says R207,00, VAT included. To find the price before tax, DIVIDE by 1,15 — back to R180 exactly. Never take 15 percent off the total; the tax was charged on the smaller number. And the stall: a vetkoek costs R4,00 to make, sells at R7,00. Mark-up isn't 42,9 percent — it's 3 over 4, a full 75 percent, measured against what SHE paid. Finance and Data power most of the money-and-numbers marks in this subject — and these are exactly the moves that earn them.
visual_style: A homework book on a kitchen table, marks rearranging themselves into order; a red outlier mark dragging a see-saw labelled MEAN while a steady pin labelled MEDIAN holds still; a till slip splitting into 180 and 27; vetkoek stacking into a percentage bar.
mood: Family-kitchen real talk, sharp and reassuring.
pacing: Quick homework-book setup, a beat on the 60-versus-68 argument, brisk VAT and mark-up finishes with numbers landing like till beeps.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and walk into your finals knowing exactly where the money marks live.
